cells.tense: The ending is here now, and you are the one holding the pen on it.
cells.ask: Name one thing that is finished and write the last sentence of it — one plain line, to yourself, no explaining.
cells.core:
You know what's done and you're willing to say so. The ending isn't being dragged out and it isn't being denied — the clearing is happening, and you're the one who decided it should. You can stand in that without flinching, and standing in it is the work: you're not rehearsing it, you're not reliving it. You're just here, with the finished thing, letting it be finished.

What got made here, with all the weight it carries, is real. It took the whole cycle to get it to the point where it could end, and the ending is part of the making, not a retreat from it. What's cultivated reaches completion. The clearing is the shape of it, and you're holding the shape.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's finished and you're willing to let it be.
cells.place: the clearing where necessary endings finish

cells.tense: You will get to the ending, and the way you are bracing for it is making it come early.
cells.ask: Close one loop that is actually closed — cancel one thing, finish one small task, say one goodbye — and do nothing else new today.
cells.core:
You're already standing at the end of the next thing. Before this clearing has even finished, you're bracing for the one after it — finishing ahead of time, tidying what isn't yours yet, trying to see what's coming so it can't surprise you. The forward lean pulls the energy out of what's actually here.

At its best, the ending lands and you're still in the room with it. The completion is real, not a rehearsal. When you live past the ending, you skip the part where the thing actually finishes — and the finishing is what makes it real. You are rushing the close, and the rush is costing you the close.
cells.sheetLine: You're finishing ahead of the ending instead of letting it finish.
cells.place: the clearing where necessary endings finish

cells.tense: You stood at the door when the ending was ready, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Receive one thing that wants to reach you — a message, an offer, a person's attention — and let it in without deciding anything about it yet.
cells.core:
The ending needed to happen and it didn't. Something stays open behind you — a yes you didn't give, a thing that finished without being said finished — and you're still holding it from the far side. The room is cleared. You haven't walked in.

At its best, it's simpler than it sounds: the door closes, and something new has ground to stand on. Right now that ground isn't there. Not from lack of effort — from the not-letting-in. When you keep the ending at arm's length, the next beginning waits. One thing received, one thing allowed to land, and the floor starts to appear.
cells.sheetLine: Something finished and you held it open anyway.
cells.place: the clearing where necessary endings finish

cells.tense: You are already clearing the ground here, though you'd say the ground cleared itself.
cells.ask: Say one ending was yours — the version you tell where it happened to you is not the whole of it.
cells.core:
The clearing is running. Things have ended under your hand — you've let go of what you've let go of, you've made the calls, you've kept going — and your account has the season doing it. The work is real; you just haven't taken it up as yours. The saying-so is what's missing, not the doing.

At its best, that part is simple: you name what you ended, and you stand behind the words. You carry what the beginning promised far enough to put it down, and putting down is a thing you did. Saying so doesn't change what happened. It gives the next thing somewhere to land, and it gives you back the hand that did it.
cells.sheetLine: The ending was yours to make. Say so once.
cells.place: the clearing where necessary endings finish
